The study uses a mouse knock-in model to demonstrate that the R719W variant causes progressive cardiac hypertrophy, fibrosis, and myofiber disarray, with homozygous animals being neonatally lethal. Although fractional shortening remained preserved at 26 weeks in heterozygotes, the morphological and survival data provide strong evidence for a pathogenic functional effect in an in vivo model.
